verses.text: The gates of Jericho were shut tight because of the Israelites. No one went out and no one came in.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Look, I have given Jericho into your hands, with its king and its strong fighters.
March around the city once with all your fighting men. Do this for six days.
Have seven priests carry seven trumpets made from rams' horns ahead of the covenant box. On the seventh day, march around the city seven times, with the priests blowing the trumpets.
When you hear them play one long blast on the trumpets, have all the people give a loud shout. Then the city wall will fall down flat, and everyone will go straight in."
So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said, "Lift up the covenant box, and have seven priests carry trumpets ahead of the LORD's box."
He told the people, "Go forward! March around the city, with the armed men going ahead of the LORD's box."
When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests with the seven trumpets went forward before the LORD, blowing their trumpets, and the LORD's covenant box followed them.
The armed men marched ahead of the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard followed the box. All this time the trumpets kept sounding.
But Joshua had told the people, "Do not shout or raise your voices. Do not say a word until the day I tell you to shout. Then shout!"
So he had the LORD's box carried around the city once. Then the people went back to camp and spent the night there.
Joshua got up early the next morning, and the priests lifted up the LORD's box.

The seven priests with the seven trumpets kept marching ahead of the LORD's box, blowing the trumpets. The armed men went in front of them, and the rear guard followed the box. The trumpets kept sounding.
On the second day they marched around the city once and went back to camp. They did this for six days.
On the seventh day they got up at dawn and marched around the city in the same way, but this time seven times. It was the only day they went around seven times.
The seventh time around, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua told the people, "Shout! The LORD has given you the city!
The city and everything in it must be set apart to the LORD for destruction. Only Rahab the prostitute and everyone with her in her house will be spared, because she hid the spies we sent.
But stay away from the things set apart for destruction. If you take any of them, you will bring destruction and trouble on the camp of Israel.
All the silver and gold, and everything made of bronze and iron, is holy to the LORD. It must go into the LORD's treasury."
So the priests blew the trumpets, and the people shouted. When they heard the trumpet sound and gave a loud shout, the wall fell down flat. Everyone charged straight in, and they took the city.
With their swords they destroyed everything in the city: men and women, young and old, cattle, sheep and donkeys.
Joshua told the two men who had spied out the land, "Go into the prostitute's house and bring her out with all her family, as you promised her."

So the young spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers and all who belonged to her. They brought out her whole family and put them in a place outside the camp of Israel.
Then they burned the whole city and everything in it. But they put the silver, the gold, and the things made of bronze and iron into the treasury of the LORD's house.
Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, her family and all who belonged to her. She lives among the Israelites to this day, because she hid the men Joshua sent to spy on Jericho.

At that time Joshua made the people take this oath: "May the man who tries to rebuild the city of Jericho be cursed before the LORD. His oldest son will die when he lays its foundations, and his youngest son will die when he sets up its gates."
So the LORD was with Joshua, and he became famous all through the land.
